text:
sara: quick help — Marta moved from Berlin to Lisbon and switched payroll mid-pay period. She relocated on 2024-08-14; pay period is 2024-08-01 -> 2024-08-31. Contract switched to PT payroll effective 2024-08-15. How should we handle income tax and social contributions for the August payrun and year-end docs?

oliver_payroll: short answer: we should split the period and run two payslips (DE for 8/1-8/14, PT for 8/15-8/31). need to confirm a few things first: 1) Marta's official tax residency change date, 2) whether employer continued DE SS for the first half, and 3) any A1 or social security certificates. do we have her de-registration date?

juan_pp: @sara Marta told me she deregistered Berlin (Abmeldung) on 2024-08-14 evening and registered in PT on 2024-08-15. She sent a copy of the Portuguese NIF and temporary residency note. No A1 on file.

oliver_payroll: ok helpful. Without an A1, German social security contributions likely apply up to 8/14 (employer side + employee). For PT we run contributions from 8/15 onwards. For taxes: Germany will tax income earned while tax resident/working there; Portugal will tax income from the PT payroll period. We must ensure we don't double-withhold for the same income.

marta: fyi I asked my manager about A1 — they were told the secondment was long-term so they didn't request one, sorry.

oliver_payroll: that's fine — we treat it as a change of payroll. Action items: 1) Create two payslips for Aug (DE gross for 1–14, PT gross for 15–31). 2) Collect proof of de-registration/registration to support tax residency boundary. 3) Run retro withhold if DE payroll didn't withhold enough. 4) Flag for local tax filing guidance.

sara: can you outline how the numbers should be split? i.e., do we prorate the monthly salary by days or by working days?

oliver_payroll: we prorate by calendar days in practice unless contract specifies otherwise. Example snippet:

```
monthly_gross: €6,000
period_DE_days: 14 => DE_gross = 6000 * 14/31 = €2709.68
period_PT_days: 17 => PT_gross = 6000 * 17/31 = €3290.32
```

oliver_payroll: social security: calculate DE contributions on DE_gross, PT contributions on PT_gross. If employer previously withheld any 'year-to-date' thresholds (e.g., social ceilings) need manual review.

juan_pp: for year-end docs: Germany will issue a final Lohnsteuerbescheinigung for the DE period, Portugal will issue the equivalent (declaração de remunerações/IRS reporting) for the PT period. We should produce a combined summary for the employee for cross-border filing support.

marta: will this affect my end-of-year home country filings? i.e., I normally file German tax return — do I need to include Portuguese income too?

juan_pp: yes — if you are tax resident in PT for part of the year you'll likely need to file in both jurisdictions and claim foreign income credits where applicable. Recommend local tax advisor. We can provide payroll docs and the day-split evidence.

oliver_payroll: operational next steps (assigned to payroll ops):
- upload Marta's de-registration and PT registration to the case file
- create DE payslip for 1–14 (run immediate retro if DE payroll not processed)
- create PT payslip for 15–31 on PT tenant, ensure correct NIF and social base
- mark in HRIS: tax residency change date = 2024-08-15
- add note for year-end docs and create combined earnings summary PDF

payroll-bot: PAYROLL_RUN CHECK — DE retro-run queued (job id: pr-202408-194860). ETA 2 business days.

sara: thanks. who should I loop in for legal/compliance on social security risk?

oliver_payroll: loop in paula_compliance and our EMEA legal; also ping external payroll vendor in PT for local nuance on contributions ceilings. I'll create the ticket in Payroll Ops and tag people-ops.

juan_pp: i'll DM Marta the checklist of docs to upload. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
